items.title: Natural body proportions
items.content: WHEN: A person appears in the picture. DO: Give a realistic head to body ratio, normal arm and leg length and a believable height next to the furniture and the room. DO NOT: Stretch, elongate or distort the body.

items.title: Clear natural skin
items.content: WHEN: A face or skin is visible. DO: Show clear, even skin with no acne, pimples, spots or scars, yet natural with visible pores. DO NOT: Make skin waxy, plastic or heavily retouched.

items.title: Looks like a phone photo
items.content: WHEN: Making or checking any keyframe. DO: Make it look like an ordinary photo taken with a phone: natural light, a little grain, everyday details of a lived-in home. DO NOT: Make it glossy, retouched, studio or 3D-render looking.

items.title: One story told in different shots
items.content: WHEN: Writing the script and cutting it into shots. DO: Tell one story in this order: a hook, a problem shoppers know, the product solving it, one or two concrete benefits, a call to open the product link. Give the shots these roles in order: hook, problem, demo, benefit, call_to_action (with fewer than five shots merge neighbouring roles, with more shots repeat demo or benefit; the first shot is always the hook and the last always the call_to_action). Each shot follows from the one before (cause and effect), and the voiceovers read in order give the script with nothing added or repeated. Open the first shot on a close-up of the product or a problem shoppers know, with movement already in the very first frame, put a short on-screen question or claim in its on_screen_text, and end on the result: the last shot shows the state after use in a framing, camera angle and action clearly different from the first shot. Change the camera angle, the distance and the action between shots, and where the story needs it the spot inside the same home. DO NOT: Start a new topic in a later shot, open on a still or empty frame, add shots just to fill every role, or make shots that only zoom or drift or look alike in framing, camera movement or action (it would play like a slideshow).

items.title: What the voice says
items.content: WHEN: Writing any voiceover. DO: Open the first shot on a situation or question the shopper knows from daily life, such as a problem they just had, so the product answers something they already feel. Give the reason, the benefit or the feeling that the picture cannot show, and let the picture show the look, the shape and the action; every sentence must tell the shopper something new. When a size, a quantity, a duration or a price from the product facts is spoken, follow it at once with what it means in everyday life, worked out only from the same facts (a 300 ml bottle fills a big glass, a 40 cm length reaches the knee). DO NOT: Open with a greeting, an introduction or an announcement (chào mọi người, hôm nay mình review, sau đây mình sẽ giới thiệu), describe what is already on screen (ở đây các bạn thấy, nhìn vào đây), repeat a point already made, add a sentence only to fill the time, recite a bare figure, or let a meaning add a benefit or result that the product facts do not state.

items.title: How the voice is written
items.content: WHEN: Writing or checking any voiceover or script. DO: Write the way a young Vietnamese seller talks to a friend on TikTok: short sentences and plain everyday words, in a natural tone. Cut the speech into sentences of 12 words or fewer, with a comma or a full stop at least every 8 words, so the voice pauses naturally. Write every number in words as it is read aloud (hai trăm sáu mươi tám mi-li-lít, không 268ml). DO NOT: Use written, Sino-Vietnamese or advertising words (cao cấp, sang trọng, đẳng cấp, tối ưu, sở hữu), slang or filler particles added only to sound casual, digits, or English words a speaker would have to read out.

items.title: Voiceover length of each shot
items.content: WHEN: Writing the voiceover of a shot. DO: Each shot lasts 15 seconds and the video follows the length of the voice, so write the voiceover of every shot as about 62 Vietnamese words (never below 56 or above 70), which the voice reads in about 12 to 13 seconds, enough to fill nearly the whole shot; count the words of each shot before answering and lengthen a shot that is short with one more concrete detail of the story, never with filler; this holds for a shot where the person talks to the camera as well. DO NOT: Write a short line that leaves the paid clip mostly unused and the video much shorter than planned, or a line so long that it runs past the end of the shot.

items.title: Keyframe prompt reads like a phone photo
items.content: WHEN: Writing a keyframe_prompt. DO: Describe an ordinary photo taken on a phone: natural window or room light, a little grain, a lived-in Vietnamese home with everyday clutter, natural skin and hair; say what is seen (action, framing, distance, camera angle). Keep the real product clearly visible and recognisable from the first frame to the last, held, worn, placed or in use. When a person is in the shot, frame the face and mouth in the middle of the picture, above the lower third where the spoken words appear and away from the top left corner where price stickers slide in. DO NOT: Use perfect, flawless, cinematic, stunning, studio, professional, glossy or 8k, vague mood words, or show a product version other than product_variant; hide the product, crop it out or let it become tiny; put the mouth, chin or the product's label in the lower third or in the top left corner, where a caption or sticker would cover it.

items.title: Motion prompt as timed beats
items.content: WHEN: Writing a motion_prompt for a 15 second clip. DO: Name the subject in a few words, then write four or five sentences as timed beats of about 3 seconds, each a new clearly visible action or camera move; name the shot size, camera height and every move with its exact term (dolly, zoom, pan, tilt, tracking, orbit, handheld); keep one continuous camera path with brisk TikTok-style energy; for a narrated shot lips stay closed or relaxed, for a talking shot the person talks naturally. DO NOT: Re-describe the face, outfit or product, use mood words, add sound or music, cut scenes, add new objects, refer to an icon, button, sticker or any on-screen graphic (the clip has none, so the model would draw one; point at a place in the frame instead), or use slow motion or a slow drift.

items.title: Safe, grounded claims
items.content: WHEN: Writing any text, voiceover or on-screen text. DO: Take every number, percentage, price, material and feature from the product facts. DO NOT: Invent figures or features, use absolute claims (tốt nhất, rẻ nhất, số 1, 100%, chắc chắn), name other shopping or social platforms, promise medical results, or promise a gift or reward for tapping the link.
